title: Expert-level detection of low-voltage intervals in EEG as a robust biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy
abstract: arXiv:2610.12680v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Background: Discontinuity in neonatal EEG is a critical marker of brain dysfunction but can be difficult to quantify visually. Inter-burst intervals (IBIs) are a key characteristic of discontinuity, yet their definition does not easily translate to AI detection. Objectives: To introduce low-voltage intervals (LVIs), defined exclusively by amplitude and duration, as a context-independent alternative to IBIs, develop an AI detection method for LVIs, and assess their clinical utility as a marker of brain injury. Methods: We developed a ConvNeXt model to detect LVIs and compared its performance with existing methods. We then tested the clinical relevance of detected LVIs across four applications: 1) grading background EEG abnormalities on an open benchmark dataset, 2) classifying clinical hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) grades and comparing with a normal EEG dataset, 3) seizure prediction, and 4) association with seizure burden. translated_title: 脑电图低电压间期的专家级检测：一种新生儿脑病的稳健生物标志物
translated_abstract: 背景：新生儿脑电图的不连续性是脑功能障碍的关键标志，但难以通过视觉观察进行量化。爆发间期（IBIs）是衡量不连续性的一个关键特征，然而其定义不易直接转化为AI检测任务。研究目标：本文引入低电压间期（LVIs）这一概念，其仅由振幅和持续时间定义，作为IBI的独立于上下文的替代方案；开发一种针对LVIs的AI检测方法，并评估其作为脑损伤标志物的临床实用性。方法：我们开发了一个ConvNeXt模型来检测LVIs，并将其性能与现有方法进行比较。随后，我们在四项应用中检验了所检测LVIs的临床相关性：1）在一个公开基准数据集上对脑电图背景异常进行分级；2）对临床缺氧缺血性脑病（HIE）分级并与正常脑电图数据集进行对比；3）癫痫发作预测；4）与癫痫发作负荷的关联分析。结果：（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出仅由振幅和持续时间定义的低电压间期（LVIs）作为新生儿脑电图不连续性的全新指标，并开发了基于ConvNeXt的AI检测模型，在异常分级、HIE分级、癫痫预测等多项任务中验证了LVIs作为新生儿脑病稳健生物标志物的专家级检测能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces low-voltage intervals (LVIs), defined solely by amplitude and duration, as a context-independent alternative to inter-burst intervals in neonatal EEG, and develops a ConvNeXt-based AI model achieving expert-level detection of LVIs, validating their utility as a robust biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy across grading, HIE classification, and seizure prediction tasks.
